nodes.label: Circle Construction with Given Radius
nodes.title: Drawing a circle with a specified radius using a compass.

nodes.label: Transferring a Length with a Compass
nodes.title: Using a compass to copy a given distance from one location to another.

nodes.label: Constructing an Angle of Given Measure with a Protractor
nodes.title: Drawing an angle with a specified degree measure using a protractor.

nodes.label: Drawing Perpendicular Lines with a Set Square
nodes.title: Using a set square to construct a line perpendicular to a given line.

nodes.label: Drawing Parallel Lines with a Set Square
nodes.title: Using a set square to construct a line parallel to a given line.

nodes.label: Drawing a Straight Line Through Two Points with a Straightedge
nodes.title: Using a straightedge to join two points with a straight line segment.

nodes.label: Measuring Line Segments with a Ruler
nodes.title: Using a ruler to measure the length of a segment to a specified unit and precision.

nodes.label: Measuring Angles with a Protractor
nodes.title: Using a protractor to determine the degree measure of an angle.

nodes.label: Geometric Constructions in Dynamic Geometry Software
nodes.title: Constructing and manipulating geometric figures using dynamic geometry tools while preserving constraints.

nodes.label: Interpreting Slope as Rate of Change
nodes.title: Recognizing that the slope of a linear graph equals the rate of change of the dependent variable per unit change in the independent variable, with contextual units.

nodes.label: Interpreting y-Intercept as Start Value
nodes.title: Identifying the y-intercept as the initial value when the independent variable is zero and interpreting its meaning in context.

nodes.label: Point of Intersection of Two Linear Graphs as Common Solution
nodes.title: Understanding that the intersection of two linear graphs gives the values that satisfy both relationships and interpreting that solution in real-life contexts.

nodes.label: Graphing Linear Relationships
nodes.title: Plotting points and drawing straight-line graphs from a table or slope-intercept form to represent a linear relationship.

nodes.label: Representing Linear Relationships in Tables
nodes.title: Creating or reading tables of input-output pairs that model a linear rule derived from a context or equation.

nodes.label: Calculating Slope from Two Points
nodes.title: Computing slope using m = (y2 − y1)/(x2 − x1) from coordinates or tabular data and interpreting the result.

nodes.label: Comparing Linear Relationships by Rate of Change and Start Value
nodes.title: Using slopes and y-intercepts to compare which relationship changes faster and which has a higher initial value.

nodes.label: Constructing Linear Models from Real-Life Contexts
nodes.title: Determining the rate of change and start value from a situation and expressing the relationship in y = mx + b form.

nodes.label: Solving a System of Two Linear Equations by Graphing
nodes.title: Graphing both linear relationships and reading their point of intersection to find the simultaneous solution.

nodes.label: Solving Linear Problems Using Tables (Numeric Strategy)
nodes.title: Using tabulated values to compute outputs, compare relationships, and locate approximate intersections numerically.

nodes.label: Plotting Points in the Cartesian Plane
nodes.title: Placing ordered pairs on the coordinate axes and reading coordinates accurately to support graphing.

nodes.label: Mental Estimation in Linear Contexts
nodes.title: Estimating values, rates, or intersection points using slopes and intercepts without full computation.

nodes.label: Applying the Pythagorean Theorem to Right Triangles
nodes.title: Using a^2 + b^2 = c^2 to determine unknown side lengths and distances in right-angled triangle problems, including simple heights-and-distances contexts.

nodes.label: Solving Right Triangle Word Problems with Trigonometric Ratios
nodes.title: Modeling real-world situations involving angles as right triangles and selecting sine, cosine, or tangent to find unknown sides or angles.

nodes.label: Sine Ratio in Right Triangles
nodes.title: Defining and using sin(θ) = opposite/hypotenuse for an acute angle in a right triangle.

nodes.label: Cosine Ratio in Right Triangles
nodes.title: Defining and using cos(θ) = adjacent/hypotenuse for an acute angle in a right triangle.

nodes.label: Tangent Ratio in Right Triangles
nodes.title: Defining and using tan(θ) = opposite/adjacent for an acute angle in a right triangle.

nodes.label: Inverse Trigonometric Functions for Angle Calculation
nodes.title: Using arcsin, arccos, and arctan to find acute angles from given side ratios in right triangles.

nodes.label: Angles of Elevation and Depression
nodes.title: Interpreting and defining angles measured from the horizontal line of sight to set up trigonometric models for height and distance problems.

nodes.label: Identifying Opposite, Adjacent, and Hypotenuse
nodes.title: Determining triangle sides relative to a given acute angle in a right triangle to choose the appropriate trigonometric ratio.

nodes.label: Enlargement (Dilation) in the Plane
nodes.title: Transforming a figure by scaling distances from a fixed center by a rational factor k, with k>1 enlarging and 0<k<1 reducing.

nodes.label: Center of Enlargement
nodes.title: The fixed point from which all points are scaled radially during a dilation.

nodes.label: Scale Factor of an Enlargement
nodes.title: The rational constant k that determines the ratio of image to preimage lengths in a dilation (k>1 enlarges, 0<k<1 reduces).

nodes.label: Area Scaling Under Enlargement
nodes.title: Under a dilation with scale factor k, the area of a figure is multiplied by k^2.

nodes.label: Translation in the Plane
nodes.title: An isometry that slides every point of a figure by a given vector without rotation or reflection.

nodes.label: Rotation about a Point
nodes.title: An isometry that turns a figure through a specified angle and direction around a fixed center.

nodes.label: Axial Symmetry (Reflection Across a Line)
nodes.title: Reflecting a point or figure across a line so that the line is the perpendicular bisector of each segment joining corresponding points.

nodes.label: Central Symmetry (Point Reflection)
nodes.title: Reflecting a point or figure through a center so that the center is the midpoint of each segment joining corresponding points.

nodes.label: Locating Axes of Symmetry in Simple Shapes
nodes.title: Identifying lines that map a shape onto itself under reflection.

nodes.label: Mathematical Proof
nodes.title: A logical argument that demonstrates the truth of a geometric statement from axioms and previously proven results.

nodes.label: Proof by Contradiction
nodes.title: A proof technique that assumes the negation of the desired statement and derives a contradiction, thereby proving the original statement.

nodes.label: Theorem
nodes.title: A mathematical statement proven true using axioms, definitions, and prior theorems.

nodes.label: Axiom
nodes.title: A fundamental assumption accepted without proof, serving as a starting point for geometric reasoning.

nodes.label: Corollary
nodes.title: A result that follows readily from a theorem, often requiring little or no additional proof.

nodes.label: Converse of a Theorem
nodes.title: The statement formed by reversing the hypothesis and conclusion of an implication; may or may not be true.

nodes.label: If and Only If (Biconditional)
nodes.title: A statement asserting two implications hold, establishing logical equivalence between conditions.

nodes.label: Logical Implication
nodes.title: The relationship where one statement guarantees the truth of another, typically written as 'if P, then Q'.

nodes.label: Slope of a Line
nodes.title: Calculating the gradient of a line from two points as (y2−y1)/(x2−x1) or from ax+by+c=0 as −a/b when b≠0.

nodes.label: Slope Criteria for Parallel Lines
nodes.title: Two non-vertical lines are parallel if and only if their slopes are equal; vertical lines are parallel to each other.

nodes.label: Slope Criteria for Perpendicular Lines
nodes.title: Two non-vertical lines are perpendicular if and only if the product of their slopes is −1; vertical lines are perpendicular to horizontal lines.

nodes.label: Angle Between Two Lines
nodes.title: Finding the acute angle θ between lines with slopes m1 and m2 using tanθ = |(m2−m1)/(1+m1m2)|, with special handling for vertical lines.

nodes.label: Perpendicular Distance from a Point to a Line
nodes.title: Computing the shortest distance from (x0,y0) to ax+by+c=0 using |ax0+by0+c|/√(a^2+b^2).

nodes.label: General Form of a Linear Equation
nodes.title: Recognizing and using ax+by+c=0 as the equation of a straight line and converting between general and slope-intercept forms.

nodes.label: Circle Equation in Center-Radius Form
nodes.title: Representing a circle with center (h,k) and radius r by (x−h)^2+(y−k)^2=r^2 and identifying points on the circle.

nodes.label: General Form of a Circle Equation
nodes.title: Recognizing x^2+y^2+2gx+2fy+c=0 as a circle with center (−g,−f) and radius r=√(g^2+f^2−c).

nodes.label: Intersection of a Line and a Circle
nodes.title: Solving a line–circle system by substitution to find 0, 1, or 2 intersection points; using the discriminant to determine the number of solutions.

nodes.label: Internal Division of a Line Segment
nodes.title: Finding the coordinates of the point that divides a segment joining (x1,y1) and (x2,y2) internally in the ratio m:n.

nodes.label: Area of a Triangle in the Coordinate Plane
nodes.title: Computing area from vertices (x1,y1), (x2,y2), (x3,y3) using the determinant formula A=1/2|x1(y2−y3)+x2(y3−y1)+x3(y1−y2)|.

nodes.label: Unit Circle Definition of Sine and Cosine
nodes.title: Defines sinθ and cosθ for all real θ using the x- and y-coordinates of a point on the unit circle, establishing periodicity and quadrant signs.

nodes.label: Definition of Tangent Function
nodes.title: Defines tanθ as sinθ/cosθ with domain restrictions where cosθ = 0, and relates tangent to slope on the unit circle.

nodes.label: Radian Measure of Angles
nodes.title: Uses radians as the natural unit for angle measure and converts between degrees and radians; connects arc length via θ = s/r.

nodes.label: Sine Rule
nodes.title: Applies a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C to find unknown sides or angles in any triangle, including ambiguous cases.

nodes.label: Cosine Rule
nodes.title: Uses c^2 = a^2 + b^2 − 2ab cos C (and cyclic forms) to determine unknown sides or angles in any triangle.

nodes.label: Area of a Triangle via Trigonometry
nodes.title: Computes area using K = 1/2 ab sin C (or cyclic variants) when two sides and the included angle are known.

nodes.label: Arc Length in Radians
nodes.title: Calculates arc length of a circle sector with s = rθ when θ is in radians.

nodes.label: Area of a Sector
nodes.title: Finds the area of a sector using A = 1/2 r^2 θ for θ in radians.

nodes.label: Graphing Sine Function
nodes.title: Plots y = sin θ, identifying amplitude, period 2π, intercepts, symmetry, and key points.

nodes.label: Graphing Cosine Function
nodes.title: Plots y = cos θ, identifying amplitude, period 2π, intercepts, symmetry, and key points.

nodes.label: Graphing Tangent Function
nodes.title: Plots y = tan θ with period π, vertical asymptotes at θ = π/2 + kπ, and symmetry properties.

nodes.label: Graphing y = a + b sin(cθ)
nodes.title: Graphs transformed sine functions with vertical shift a, amplitude |b|, and period 2π/|c|.

nodes.label: Graphing y = a + b cos(cθ)
nodes.title: Graphs transformed cosine functions with vertical shift a, amplitude |b|, and period 2π/|c|.

nodes.label: Solving sin(nθ) = 0 (All Solutions)
nodes.title: Finds the general solution θ = kπ/n for integer k, accounting for the periodicity of sine.

nodes.label: Solving cos(nθ) = 1/2 (All Solutions)
nodes.title: Finds general solutions using reference angles: nθ = ±π/3 + 2kπ, hence θ = (±π/3 + 2kπ)/n.

nodes.label: Trigonometric Problem Solving in 3D
nodes.title: Applies right-triangle trigonometry and Pythagoras in three dimensions to determine distances, heights, and angles.

nodes.label: Pythagoras' Theorem in 2D Problem Solving
nodes.title: Uses a^2 + b^2 = c^2 to find unknown side lengths and to verify right angles in plane figures.

nodes.label: Exact Trigonometric Values in Surd Form
nodes.title: Works with exact values of trig ratios for special angles (e.g., 30°, 45°, 60°) expressed using radicals.

nodes.label: Enlargement (Dilation) Transformation
nodes.title: A similarity transformation that maps a figure to a proportional image using a specified center and positive scale factor k.

nodes.label: Centre of Enlargement
nodes.title: The fixed point from which all distances to points on a figure are multiplied by the scale factor during an enlargement.

nodes.label: Scale Factor in Enlargement
nodes.title: A positive number k that multiplies distances from the center to produce the image; determines whether the image is a magnification or reduction.

nodes.label: Area Scale Factor under Enlargement
nodes.title: In two dimensions, the area of the image is k^2 times the area of the original when enlarged by scale factor k.

nodes.label: Enlargements with Scale Factor k>1
nodes.title: Magnifications where k>1 produce an image larger than the original while preserving shape.

nodes.label: Reductions with Scale Factor 0<k<1
nodes.title: Reductions where 0<k<1 produce an image smaller than the original while preserving shape.

nodes.label: Using Rational Scale Factors in Enlargements
nodes.title: Applying enlargements with k ∈ Q, including computing corresponding lengths and areas with fractional scale factors.

nodes.label: Constructing an Enlargement Given Centre and Scale Factor
nodes.title: Produce the image by joining points to the center and multiplying each center-to-point distance by k.

nodes.label: Determining the Scale Factor from Object and Image
nodes.title: Calculate k as the ratio of corresponding lengths (or distances from the center) between the image and the original.

nodes.label: Locating the Centre of Enlargement from Object and Image
nodes.title: Find the center as the intersection point of lines through pairs of corresponding points of the object and its image.

nodes.label: Set of Rational Numbers (Q)
nodes.title: Numbers that can be expressed as a fraction a/b where a and b are integers and b ≠ 0.

nodes.label: Equivalence of Fractions, Decimals, and Percentages
nodes.title: Recognising and converting between fractions, decimals (terminating or repeating), and percentages as representations of the same rational number.

nodes.label: Addition and Subtraction of Rational Numbers
nodes.title: Performing addition and subtraction with fractions, decimals, and percentages while preserving arithmetic properties and using strategies like common denominators or number lines.

nodes.label: Multiplication and Division of Rational Numbers
nodes.title: Carrying out multiplication and division of fractions and decimals, including invert-and-multiply for fraction division.

nodes.label: Ordering Rational Numbers on the Number Line
nodes.title: Placing rational numbers on the number line and comparing their order and magnitude.

nodes.label: Number Line Models for Rational Addition and Subtraction
nodes.title: Using directed segments on the number line to model and compute addition and subtraction of rational numbers.

nodes.label: Set of Integers (Z)
nodes.title: All whole numbers including negative numbers, zero, and positive numbers.

nodes.label: Integer Addition with Negative Numbers
nodes.title: Adding integers using sign rules and number line interpretations of directed quantities.

nodes.label: Integer Subtraction with Negative Numbers
nodes.title: Subtracting integers by adding the additive inverse and interpreting direction on the number line.

nodes.label: Integer Multiplication with Negative Numbers (Sign Rules)
nodes.title: Applying sign rules for products of integers: same signs give positive, different signs give negative.

nodes.label: Integer Division with Negative Numbers (Sign Rules)
nodes.title: Applying sign rules for quotients of integers: same signs give positive, different signs give negative.

nodes.label: Justifying Integer Sign Rules Using Properties of Arithmetic
nodes.title: Deriving and explaining sign rules for multiplication and division using the distributive property and additive inverses.

nodes.label: Order of Operations with Brackets
nodes.title: Evaluating expressions by following the agreed order of operations and using brackets to specify grouping.

nodes.label: Commutative Property of Addition and Multiplication
nodes.title: The order of numbers does not affect sums or products (a+b=b+a, ab=ba); does not hold for subtraction or division.

nodes.label: Associative Property of Addition and Multiplication
nodes.title: The grouping of addends or factors does not change the sum or product (e.g., (a+b)+c=a+(b+c)).

nodes.label: Distributive Law of Multiplication over Addition
nodes.title: Multiplication distributes over addition: a(b+c)=ab+ac; used to reason about operations, including with negatives.

nodes.label: Number Line Models for Integer Operations
nodes.title: Using the number line to illustrate integer addition, subtraction, and the effect of scaling for multiplication.

nodes.label: Set of Natural Numbers (N)
nodes.title: The counting numbers 1, 2, 3, … used to count discrete objects.

nodes.label: Decomposition Strategy for Addition and Subtraction in N
nodes.title: Breaking numbers into place-value parts to simplify mental addition and subtraction.

nodes.label: Skip Counting as a Model for Multiplication in N
nodes.title: Counting by equal increments to represent repeated addition and understand multiplication.

nodes.label: Array Model for Multiplication in N
nodes.title: Using rectangular arrays to visualise multiplication and area, supporting commutativity.

nodes.label: Equal Groups Model for Multiplication and Division in N
nodes.title: Interpreting multiplication as combining equal groups and division as partitioning or measuring equal groups.

nodes.label: Inverse Relationships: Addition–Subtraction
nodes.title: Understanding subtraction as the inverse of addition and using this relationship to check and solve problems.

nodes.label: Inverse Relationships: Multiplication–Division
nodes.title: Understanding division as the inverse of multiplication and using this relationship to check and solve problems.

nodes.label: Terminating Decimals as Rational Numbers
nodes.title: Decimals that end can be expressed exactly as fractions and thus are rational numbers.

nodes.label: Repeating Decimals as Rational Numbers
nodes.title: Decimals with a repeating pattern correspond to fractions and are rational numbers.

nodes.label: Percentages as Rational Numbers
nodes.title: A percent represents parts per hundred and can be written as a fraction with denominator 100.

nodes.label: Contextual Interpretation of Negative Numbers (Debt, Temperature)
nodes.title: Using real-life contexts to interpret and reason about negative values and direction.

nodes.label: Solving Contextual Problems with Fractional Amounts
nodes.title: Representing and solving real-world problems that involve fractions, decimals, or percentages.

nodes.label: Hierarchy of Number Systems (N, Z, Q, R, C)
nodes.title: Understand the standard number sets, their definitions, and inclusion relationships from natural numbers up to complex numbers.

nodes.label: Recognizing Irrational Numbers
nodes.title: Identify numbers that cannot be expressed as a ratio of integers and appreciate that the set of real numbers is not equal to the set of rational numbers (R ≠ Q).

nodes.label: Representing Real Numbers on the Number Line
nodes.title: Place and interpret natural, integer, rational, and real numbers on a number line.

nodes.label: Complex Number Arithmetic in Rectangular Form
nodes.title: Perform addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division with complex numbers written as a + ib.

nodes.label: Plotting Complex Numbers on an Argand Diagram
nodes.title: Represent a complex number a + ib as the point (a, b) in the complex plane.

nodes.label: Complex Number Modulus as Distance
nodes.title: Interpret and compute the modulus |a+ib| = √(a² + b²) as the distance from the origin on the Argand diagram.

nodes.label: Complex Conjugate and Algebraic Properties
nodes.title: Calculate the conjugate of a complex number and use properties such as conjugate of a sum and product: overline(z+w)=overline(z)+overline(w), overline(zw)=overline(z)·overline(w).

nodes.label: Order of Operations (Including Brackets)
nodes.title: Apply the conventional precedence rules for arithmetic operations, ensuring correct use of parentheses.

nodes.label: Expressing Numbers as Products of Prime Factors
nodes.title: Decompose integers into prime factors using methods such as factor trees or repeated division.

nodes.label: Determining Factors and Multiples in N
nodes.title: Identify factors and multiples of natural numbers and use divisibility rules where appropriate.

nodes.label: Scientific Notation a×10^n (1 ≤ a < 10, n ∈ Z)
nodes.title: Express non-zero positive rational numbers in normalized scientific notation.

nodes.label: Operations with Scientific Notation
nodes.title: Perform addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division on numbers written in scientific notation.

nodes.label: Expressing Decimals as Equivalent Fractions
nodes.title: Convert decimal numbers to equivalent fractions, reinforcing place value and fraction-decimal connections.

nodes.label: Geometric Construction of √2
nodes.title: Construct the length √2 using geometric methods (e.g., the diagonal of a unit square) and mark it on the number line.

nodes.label: Geometric Construction of √3
nodes.title: Construct the length √3 using right triangles and the Pythagorean theorem and represent it on the number line.

nodes.label: Proof of Irrationality of √2
nodes.title: Show that √2 cannot be expressed as a ratio of integers, typically by contradiction using parity arguments.

nodes.label: Mathematical Induction Proof Method
nodes.title: Prove statements indexed by natural numbers using base case verification and an inductive step.

nodes.label: Sum of the First n Natural Numbers Formula
nodes.title: Establish and use 1+2+…+n = n(n+1)/2.

nodes.label: Geometric Sequences and nth Term
nodes.title: Define and work with geometric sequences where a_n = ar^{n−1}.

nodes.label: Sum of a Finite Geometric Series
nodes.title: Use S_n = a(1 − r^n)/(1 − r) for r ≠ 1 to compute finite geometric sums.

nodes.label: Sum to Infinity of a Geometric Series by Limits
nodes.title: Derive and apply S_∞ = a/(1 − r) for |r| < 1 via the limit of partial sums.

nodes.label: Limit Laws for Sequences
nodes.title: Apply rules for limits of sums, products, and quotients of sequences when limits exist.

nodes.label: Limit of 1/n Approaches 0
nodes.title: Recognize by inspection that lim_{n→∞} 1/n = 0.

nodes.label: Limit of r^n for |r| < 1
nodes.title: Recognize that lim_{n→∞} r^n = 0 when the common ratio satisfies |r| < 1.

nodes.label: Converting Recurring Decimals to Fractions via Geometric Series
nodes.title: Model repeating decimals as geometric series to express them as rational numbers.

nodes.label: Derivation of Mortgage Repayment (Annuity) Formula
nodes.title: Use geometric series to derive the fixed payment formula for a level-payment loan.

nodes.label: Bernoulli's Inequality (1+x)^n ≥ 1+nx for x > −1
nodes.title: State and prove Bernoulli's inequality, often via induction, and apply it to bounds.

nodes.label: Divisibility of 4^n − 1 by 3
nodes.title: Prove that 3 divides 4^n − 1 for all natural numbers n, using induction or modular arithmetic.

nodes.label: Converting Between Fractions, Decimals, and Percentages
nodes.title: Transforming rational numbers among fraction, decimal, and percent forms to show equivalence.

nodes.label: Calculating Percentages
nodes.title: Finding a percentage of a quantity and determining percentage increase/decrease or part-to-whole percent.

nodes.label: Comparing Proportions Using Equivalent Representations
nodes.title: Comparing ratios or parts of a whole by expressing them as common fractions, decimals, or percentages.

nodes.label: Relationship Between Ratio and Proportion
nodes.title: Understanding a proportion as an equation stating two ratios are equal and using it to solve problems.

nodes.label: Recognizing Prime Numbers in N
nodes.title: Determining whether a natural number is prime using divisibility rules and the definition of prime.

nodes.label: Identifying Factors of Natural Numbers
nodes.title: Finding all positive divisors of a natural number using factor pairs and divisibility.

nodes.label: Identifying Multiples of Natural Numbers
nodes.title: Generating or testing multiples of a given natural number within a range.

nodes.label: Scientific Notation for Positive Rational Numbers
nodes.title: Expressing non-zero positive rational numbers in the form a×10^n with 1 ≤ a < 10 and n an integer, and converting to and from decimal form.

nodes.label: Rounding to a Specified Degree of Accuracy
nodes.title: Rounding results to stated decimal places or significant figures as required by a problem.

nodes.label: Estimation and Approximation of Calculations
nodes.title: Making and justifying estimates for operations using compatible numbers and strategic rounding.

nodes.label: Order-of-Magnitude Check for Results
nodes.title: Assessing whether an answer is reasonable by comparing its scale to expected powers of ten or rough bounds.

nodes.label: Verifying Solutions by Working Backwards
nodes.title: Checking a result by reversing operations or substituting into the original expressions to confirm correctness.

nodes.label: Equality as a Relation Between Expressions
nodes.title: Interpreting the equality symbol as asserting that two expressions have the same value and preserving equality under valid transformations.

nodes.label: Square of a Number (Exponent 2)
nodes.title: Interpreting and calculating a^2 as a multiplied by itself.

nodes.label: Cube of a Number (Exponent 3)
nodes.title: Interpreting and calculating a^3 as a multiplied by itself three times.

nodes.label: Square Root of a Number
nodes.title: Understanding √a as the non-negative number whose square is a; inverse of squaring.

nodes.label: Reciprocal of a Number
nodes.title: Understanding 1/a as the multiplicative inverse of a (for a ≠ 0).

nodes.label: Negative Index as Reciprocal (Exponent −1)
nodes.title: Interpreting a^−1 as the reciprocal 1/a and using the notation in calculations.

nodes.label: Fractional Index 1/2 as Square Root
nodes.title: Recognizing a^(1/2) as √a and converting between radical and index notation.

nodes.label: Sum of First n Terms of an Arithmetic Series
nodes.title: Computing S_n using formulas such as S_n = n/2 (2a + (n−1)d) or S_n = n/2 (a + l).

nodes.label: Classifying Sequences as Arithmetic, Geometric, or Neither
nodes.title: Determining whether a sequence has a constant difference, a constant ratio, or neither.

nodes.label: Finding the nth Term of an Arithmetic Sequence
nodes.title: Deriving and using the explicit formula a_n = a_1 + (n−1)d for the general term.

nodes.label: Finding the nth Term of a Geometric Sequence
nodes.title: Deriving and using the explicit formula a_n = a_1 r^{n−1} for the general term.

nodes.label: Expressing Sequence Patterns in Algebraic Form
nodes.title: Translating observed patterns into algebraic rules, including explicit or recursive formulas.

nodes.label: Extending a Sequence Based on a Given Pattern
nodes.title: Using an identified rule to continue a numeric or object sequence.

nodes.label: Generating Sequences from Term-to-Term Rules
nodes.title: Producing successive terms using an iterative process or recurrence relation.

nodes.label: Product of Powers with Same Base
nodes.title: Multiply powers with the same base by adding exponents: a^p · a^q = a^(p+q).

nodes.label: Quotient of Powers with Same Base
nodes.title: Divide powers with the same base by subtracting exponents: a^p ÷ a^q = a^(p−q), a ≠ 0.

nodes.label: Zero Exponent Rule
nodes.title: Any nonzero base raised to the zero power equals 1: a^0 = 1 for a ≠ 0.

nodes.label: Power of a Power Rule
nodes.title: Raise a power to another power by multiplying exponents: (a^p)^q = a^(pq).

nodes.label: Negative Exponent Rule
nodes.title: A negative exponent represents a reciprocal: a^(−p) = 1/a^p, a ≠ 0.

nodes.label: Power of a Product
nodes.title: Distribute an exponent over a product: (ab)^p = a^p b^p.

nodes.label: Power of a Quotient
nodes.title: Distribute an exponent over a quotient: (a/b)^p = a^p / b^p, b ≠ 0.

nodes.label: Definition of Rational Exponent 1/q
nodes.title: Relate fractional exponent to roots: a^(1/q) equals the qth root of a, with a > 0 and q ≠ 0.

nodes.label: Rational Exponent p/q Forms
nodes.title: Express a^(p/q) as (a^(1/q))^p or the qth root of a^p, with a > 0 and q ≠ 0.

nodes.label: Logarithm Product Rule
nodes.title: Log of a product is the sum of logs: log_a(xy) = log_a x + log_a y, for a > 0, a ≠ 1, x, y > 0.

nodes.label: Logarithm Quotient Rule
nodes.title: Log of a quotient is the difference of logs: log_a(x/y) = log_a x − log_a y, for a > 0, a ≠ 1, x, y > 0.

nodes.label: Logarithm Power Rule
nodes.title: Exponents come down as multipliers: log_a(x^q) = q log_a x, for a > 0, a ≠ 1, x > 0.

nodes.label: Logarithm Base and One Identities
nodes.title: Fundamental log values: log_a a = 1 and log_a 1 = 0, for a > 0 and a ≠ 1.

nodes.label: Change of Base Formula for Logarithms
nodes.title: Convert between log bases: log_a x = (log_b x) / (log_b a), with a, b > 0, a ≠ 1, b ≠ 1, x > 0.

nodes.label: Nth-Term Formula of a Sequence
nodes.title: Express the general term u(n) algebraically to describe a sequence's pattern and enable direct term calculation.

nodes.label: Extending a Sequence Using Its Pattern
nodes.title: Continue a sequence by applying its identified rule to generate subsequent terms.

nodes.label: Generating a Sequence from a Given Rule
nodes.title: Produce terms of a sequence defined by an explicit formula or a recurrence/process.

nodes.label: Exponent Product Rule
nodes.title: For the same base, multiply by adding exponents: a^p * a^q = a^(p+q) (a ≠ 0).

nodes.label: Exponent Quotient Rule
nodes.title: For the same base, divide by subtracting exponents: a^p / a^q = a^(p−q) (a ≠ 0).

nodes.label: Power of a Product Rule
nodes.title: Distribute the exponent over a product: (ab)^p = a^p b^p.

nodes.label: Power of a Quotient Rule
nodes.title: Distribute the exponent over a quotient: (b/a)^p = b^p / a^p (a ≠ 0).

nodes.label: Negative Exponent

nodes.title: Create 2D layouts of all faces of a right prism that fold to form the 3D solid, preserving edge adjacency.

nodes.title: Methods (substitution/elimination) to find common solutions to sets of linear equations.

nodes.title: Finding roots of quadratic equations by expressing as product of linear factors.

nodes.title: Formula to find roots of any quadratic equation ax^2+bx+c=0.

nodes.title: Determining the number and type of roots using the discriminant b^2 - 4ac.

nodes.title: Using substitution for systems with one linear and one quadratic equation.

nodes.title: Rewriting quadratics in the form a(x-p)^2 + q to find vertex and analyze graph properties.

nodes.title: Irrational roots expressed with radicals, including simplifying and rationalising denominators.

nodes.title: Solving equations involving square roots by isolating surds and squaring both sides, checking solutions.

nodes.title: Using known roots and long division to factorise cubic polynomials into linear and quadratic factors.

nodes.label: Radian Measure

nodes.label: Length of Arc and Area of Sector of a Circle
nodes.title: Formulas: arc length = radius × angle (in radians), sector area = 0.5 × radius² × angle.

nodes.title: Definitions of sin, cos, tan as ratios in right-angled triangles.

nodes.title: Exact values of sine, cosine and tangent for 30°, 45°, and 60°.

nodes.label: Trigonometric Functions for Angles above 90° (Unit Circle and Quadrants)
nodes.title: Using signs of trig ratios in four quadrants and reference angles to find trig values for angles beyond 90°.

nodes.label: Amplitude and Period Changes in Trigonometric Graphs
nodes.title: Effect of vertical stretch/shrink and horizontal scaling on amplitude and period of trig functions.

nodes.label: General Solutions of Trigonometric Equations
nodes.title: Finding all solutions of sin θ = k, cos θ = k, or tan θ = k using periodicity and symmetry.

nodes.label: Differential Calculus: Average Rate of Change
nodes.title: Slope of secant line between two points on a curve representing average rate of change.

nodes.label: Limits of Functions
nodes.title: Concept of limit describing the value a function approaches as the input approaches a point or infinity.

nodes.label: Differentiation from First Principles
nodes.title: Finding the derivative as the limit of difference quotients.

nodes.label: Power Rule for Differentiation
nodes.title: The derivative of x^n is n x^(n-1) for real n.

nodes.label: Sum and Difference Rule for Differentiation
nodes.title: Derivative of sum/difference equals sum/difference of derivatives.

nodes.label: Product Rule of Differentiation
nodes.title: Derivative of a product uv is u dv/dx + v du/dx.

nodes.label: Quotient Rule of Differentiation
nodes.title: Derivative of quotient u/v is (v du/dx - u dv/dx) / v^2.

nodes.label: Chain Rule of Differentiation
nodes.title: Derivative of composite function y = f(g(x)) is f'(g(x)) * g'(x).

nodes.label: Second Derivative
nodes.title: The derivative of the derivative, measuring the curvature or concavity of a function.

nodes.label: Derivatives of Basic Trigonometric Functions
nodes.title: Derivatives: d/dx(sin x) = cos x, d/dx(cos x) = -sin x, d/dx(tan x) = sec^2 x.

nodes.label: Derivatives of Inverse Trigonometric Functions
nodes.title: Derivatives of sin^-1(x), cos^-1(x), tan^-1(x) with respect to x.

nodes.label: Derivatives of Exponential Functions
nodes.title: For y = e^x, the derivative is e^x, and similarly for y = a^x.

nodes.label: Derivatives of Logarithmic Functions
nodes.title: Derivative of y = ln x is 1/x; derivatives involving log_a x.

nodes.label: Central Limit Theorem
nodes.title: For sufficiently large sample size, the sampling distribution of the sample mean is approximately normal with mean μ and standard error σ/√n, regardless of the population distribution.

nodes.label: Confidence Interval for a Population Mean (σ known)
nodes.title: Constructing a 95% confidence interval for the population mean using x̄ ± 1.96·(σ/√n), or x̄ ± z*·(σ/√n) for other confidence levels.

nodes.label: Confidence Interval for a Population Proportion
nodes.title: Estimating a population proportion using p̂ ± 1.96·√(p̂(1−p̂)/n) at the 95% confidence level.

nodes.label: Margin of Error Approximation for Proportions
nodes.title: At 95% confidence, approximating the margin of error for a sample proportion by E = 1/√n.

nodes.label: Hypothesis Test for a Population Mean (z-test)
nodes.title: Testing a claim about μ using z = (x̄ − μ)/(σ/√n), with 5% significance critical region |z| > 1.96 or p-value comparison.

nodes.label: Hypothesis Test for a Population Proportion
nodes.title: Assessing a claim about p by comparing the stated p with the 95% confidence interval for p or using a z-test for proportions.

nodes.label: p-value Interpretation in Hypothesis Testing
nodes.title: The p-value is the probability, under H0, of observing a test statistic at least as extreme as the observed; compare to α to decide significance.

nodes.label: Standard Score (z-score)
nodes.title: Standardizing a value using z = (x − μ)/σ to compare observations or compute normal probabilities.

nodes.label: Standard Normal Distribution (Z Distribution)
nodes.title: The normal distribution with mean 0 and standard deviation 1; used with Z-tables to find tail and interval probabilities.

nodes.label: Transforming Normal Variables to Z
nodes.title: Converting Normal(X ~ N(μ, σ²)) to Z via Z = (X−μ)/σ to use standard normal tables for probability calculations.

nodes.label: Empirical Rule (68-95-99.7 Rule)
nodes.title: In a normal distribution, about 68%, 95%, and 99.7% of data lie within 1, 2, and 3 standard deviations of the mean, respectively.

nodes.label: Scatter Plot Interpretation
nodes.title: Graphical display of paired quantitative data to assess form, direction, and strength of relationship.

nodes.label: Correlation Coefficient (Pearson’s r)
nodes.title: A measure (−1 to 1) of the strength and direction of linear association between two quantitative variables.

nodes.label: Line of Best Fit (Least Squares Line) by Eye
nodes.title: Drawing a straight line that best represents the trend in a scatter plot and estimating its equation y = A + Bx.

nodes.label: Correlation vs Causation
nodes.title: Understanding that a strong correlation does not imply a causal relationship between variables.

nodes.label: Binomial Distribution
nodes.title: Probability of r successes in n independent Bernoulli trials with success probability p: P(X=r)=C(n,r)p^r(1−p)^{n−r}.

nodes.label: Bernoulli Trials Model
nodes.title: A sequence of independent trials with two outcomes (success/failure) and constant probability of success.

nodes.label: Geometric Probability of First Success
nodes.title: Probability that the first success occurs on the nth trial is (1−p)^{n−1}p.

nodes.label: Negative Binomial: kth Success on nth Trial
nodes.title: Probability that the kth success occurs on the nth trial is C(n−1,k−1)p^k(1−p)^{n−k}.

nodes.label: Independence of Events
nodes.title: Events A and B are independent if P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B), equivalently P(A|B)=P(A).

nodes.label: Tree Diagrams for Compound Events
nodes.title: Diagrammatic representation of sequential events to compute joint probabilities, with or without replacement.

nodes.label: Expected Value of a Discrete Random Variable
nodes.title: The long-run average outcome of a random variable defined by E[X] = Σ x·P(x).

nodes.label: Fair Game Criterion
nodes.title: A game is fair if the player’s expected net gain is zero after accounting for cost to play.

nodes.label: Probability Simulations
nodes.title: Using random devices (dice, spinners), random number tables, or software to model probability experiments.

nodes.label: Complement Rule for 'At Least One'
nodes.title: The probability that an event occurs at least once in n trials is 1 minus the probability it never occurs.

nodes.label: Complex Numbers in Rectangular Form
nodes.title: Representation of complex numbers as z = a + bi with real part a and imaginary part b.

nodes.label: Imaginary Unit and Powers of i
nodes.title: Definition i = √−1 with i² = −1 and cyclic powers i, −1, −i, 1.

nodes.label: Addition and Subtraction of Complex Numbers
nodes.title: Add or subtract by combining real parts and imaginary parts separately.

nodes.label: Multiplication of Complex Numbers
nodes.title: Expanding (a+bi)(c+di) with i²=−1 to find the product in a+bi form.

nodes.label: Complex Conjugate and Division
nodes.title: Using the conjugate a−bi to rationalize denominators and compute quotients; z·conj(z)=|z|².

nodes.label: Equality of Complex Numbers
nodes.title: Two complex numbers are equal iff their real parts and imaginary parts are equal separately.

nodes.label: Modulus and Argument of a Complex Number
nodes.title: |z|=√(a²+b²) and arg(z)=atan2(b,a) with quadrant checks to find principal value.

nodes.label: Argand Diagram
nodes.title: Plotting complex numbers as points (a,b) in the complex plane with real and imaginary axes.

nodes.label: Polar (Modulus-Argument) Form
nodes.title: Expressing z as r(cosθ + i sinθ), where r=|z| and θ=arg(z).

nodes.label: Product and Quotient in Polar Form
nodes.title: For z1=r1(cosθ1+i sinθ1), z2=r2(cosθ2+i sinθ2): z1z2=r1r2(cos(θ1+θ2)+i sin(θ1+θ2)) and z1/z2=(r1/r2)[cos(θ1−θ2)+i sin(θ1−θ2)].

nodes.label: De Moivre’s Theorem
nodes.title: (cosθ + i sinθ)^n = cos(nθ) + i sin(nθ) for integer n; used for powers and roots of complex numbers.

nodes.label: nth Roots of a Complex Number
nodes.title: Solving z^n = a by expressing a in polar form and using De Moivre to find n distinct roots equally spaced on a circle.

nodes.label: Conjugate Roots Theorem
nodes.title: For polynomials with real coefficients, non-real complex roots occur in conjugate pairs.

nodes.label: Function, Domain, Codomain, and Range
nodes.title: A rule assigning each input in the domain to exactly one output in the codomain; the set of actual outputs is the range.

nodes.label: Vertical Line Test
nodes.title: A graph represents a function iff every vertical line intersects it at most once.

nodes.label: Composite Functions
nodes.title: Forming (g∘f)(x)=g(f(x)); generally (g∘f) ≠ (f∘g).

nodes.label: Injective, Surjective, and Bijective Functions
nodes.title: Injective: unique outputs; Surjective: every codomain element is hit; Bijective: both injective and surjective.

nodes.label: Inverse Function and Reflection in y=x
nodes.title: f^{-1} obtained by swapping x and y and solving; graph of f^{-1} is reflection of graph of f in the line y=x.

nodes.label: Quadratic Sketching by Completing the Square
nodes.title: Expressing y=ax^2+bx+c as a(x−h)^2+k to identify vertex, axis of symmetry, and shape.

nodes.label: Cubic Graph Features and Turning Points
nodes.title: Sketching cubic functions via intercepts and using the derivative to locate local maxima and minima.

nodes.label: Graph Transformations: Translations and Reflections
nodes.title: y=f(x)+a (vertical shift), y=f(x+a) (horizontal shift), y=−f(x) (reflect in x-axis), y=f(−x) (reflect in y-axis), y= k f(x) (vertical scaling).

nodes.label: Exponential Functions and Asymptotes
nodes.title: Functions of the form y = a·b^x (b>0, b≠1) with horizontal asymptote y=0 and rapid growth/decay.

nodes.label: Natural Exponential and Natural Logarithm
nodes.title: Inverse functions y=e^x and y=ln x (domain x>0), reflecting across y=x and with corresponding asymptotes.

nodes.label: Linearity of Integration
nodes.title: ∫(af(x)+bg(x)) dx = a∫f(x) dx + b∫g(x) dx for constants a, b.

nodes.label: Integrating Exponential and Trigonometric Functions
nodes.title: Formulas such as ∫e^{ax} dx = (1/a)e^{ax} + C, ∫cos(ax) dx = (1/a)sin(ax) + C, ∫sin(ax) dx = −(1/a)cos(ax) + C.

nodes.label: Antiderivative with Initial Condition
nodes.title: Finding C using a given point to determine a unique integral function satisfying a condition.

nodes.label: Definite Integral and Fundamental Theorem
nodes.title: Evaluating ∫_a^b f(x) dx via F(b)−F(a) when F′(x)=f(x).

nodes.label: Area Under a Curve and Between Curves
nodes.title: Using definite integrals to compute area with sign convention and area between curves by integrating the difference.

nodes.label: Average Value of a Function on an Interval
nodes.title: The average value over [a,b] is (1/(b−a)) ∫_a^b f(x) dx.

nodes.label: Tangent Line Using the Derivative
nodes.title: The tangent at (x1,y1) has slope f′(x1) and equation y−y1 = f′(x1)(x−x1).

nodes.label: Increasing and Decreasing Functions Test
nodes.title: A function is increasing where f′(x)>0 and decreasing where f′(x)<0.

nodes.label: Stationary Points and Second Derivative Test
nodes.title: At f′(x)=0, use f″(x)>0 for local minimum and f″(x)<0 for local maximum (subject to conditions).

nodes.label: Points of Inflection
nodes.title: Points where f″(x)=0 and changes sign; the tangent may cross the curve.

nodes.label: Optimization via Calculus
nodes.title: Finding maxima/minima of functions subject to constraints using derivatives and second derivative tests.

nodes.label: Related Rates Problems
nodes.title: Using derivatives and the chain rule to relate rates of change of linked quantities with respect to time.

nodes.label: Linear Motion with Calculus (s, v, a)
nodes.title: Connecting displacement s(t), velocity v=ds/dt, and acceleration a=dv/dt and solving motion problems via integration.

nodes.label: Compound Interest Future Value
nodes.title: Accumulated value F = P(1+i)^t for principal P at rate i per period for t periods.

nodes.label: Present Value of a Single Sum
nodes.title: Discounting a future amount F to present value P = F/(1+i)^t.

nodes.label: Effective Periodic Rate from AER
nodes.title: Finding a monthly rate r from an annual equivalent rate i via (1+r)^{12} = 1+i.

nodes.label: Reducing-Balance Depreciation
nodes.title: Asset value after t periods: F = P(1−i)^t where i is the depreciation rate per period.

nodes.label: Future Value of Instalment Savings (Annuity Due)
nodes.title: Accumulated value when depositing P at the start of each period: F = P(1+i)[(1+i)^t − 1]/i.

nodes.label: Present Value of an Annuity
nodes.title: Present value of P each period for t periods: PV = P·[1 − (1+i)^{−t}]/i (ordinary annuity; adjust for annuity due).

nodes.label: Loan/Mortgage Level Payment Formula
nodes.title: Level repayment A for loan P over t periods at rate i: A = P·[i(1+i)^t]/[(1+i)^t − 1].

nodes.label: Sector Area and Arc Length (Radians)
nodes.title: Arc length l = rθ and sector area A = (1/2)r²θ for angle θ in radians.

nodes.label: Volume and Surface Area of Cylinder, Cone, and Sphere
nodes.title: Key formulas: V_cyl=πr²h, SA_cyl=2πr²+2πrh; V_cone=(1/3)πr²h, SA_cone=πrℓ+πr²; V_sphere=(4/3)πr³, SA_sphere=4πr².

nodes.label: Frustum of a Cone Volume by Subtraction
nodes.title: Compute as volume of large cone minus small cone or use derived frustum formula.

nodes.label: Percentage Error and Tolerance
nodes.title: Quantifying measurement accuracy by relative error and instrument tolerance (± half the smallest scale unit).

nodes.label: Geometric Enlargement with Centre and Scale Factor
nodes.title: Mapping a figure to a similar figure by scaling lengths by k from a fixed centre; areas scale by k².

nodes.label: Constructing a Tangent to a Circle at a Point
nodes.title: Using the fact that the radius to the point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent line.

nodes.label: Circumcircle and Circumcenter of a Triangle
nodes.title: Perpendicular bisectors of sides meet at the circumcenter; draw circle through the triangle’s vertices.

nodes.label: Incircle and Incenter of a Triangle
nodes.title: Angle bisectors meet at the incenter; the circle tangent to all three sides has radius perpendicular to sides.

nodes.label: Centroid of a Triangle via Medians
nodes.title: Constructing medians and locating their intersection, which balances the triangle.

nodes.label: Orthocenter of a Triangle via Altitudes
nodes.title: Constructing altitudes and finding their intersection point, which may lie inside or outside the triangle.

nodes.label: Graphing Linear Functions f(x) = ax + b
nodes.title: Plotting the graph of a linear function with rational parameters a and b over real inputs.

nodes.label: Function: Unique Output for Each Input
nodes.title: Understanding that a function assigns exactly one output to every permissible input.

nodes.label: Identifying Functions Among Relations
nodes.title: Determining whether a given relation is a function based on the uniqueness of outputs for inputs.

nodes.label: Graphing Contextual Linear Relationships
nodes.title: Representing real-world linear relationships with graphs based on situations or data.

nodes.label: Function as a Well-Defined Mapping
nodes.title: Understanding a function as a rule that assigns exactly one output in the codomain to each input in the domain.

nodes.label: Function Composition (Forming Composite Functions)
nodes.title: Creating a new function (f∘g)(x) by applying one function to the output of another, with attention to domain restrictions.

nodes.label: Graphing Linear Functions y = ax + b
nodes.title: Plotting straight-line graphs using slope-intercept or two-point methods for functions of the form y = ax + b.

nodes.label: Graphing Quadratic Functions y = ax^2 + bx + c
nodes.title: Sketching parabolas by identifying key features such as vertex, axis of symmetry, and intercepts.

nodes.label: Completing the Square (Quadratic Functions)
nodes.title: Rewriting ax^2 + bx + c in vertex form a(x − h)^2 + k by adding and subtracting a square term.

nodes.label: Finding Quadratic Vertex from Completed Square Form
nodes.title: Identifying the vertex (h, k) directly from the form a(x − h)^2 + k.

nodes.label: Finding Quadratic Roots from Completed Square Form
nodes.title: Solving a(x − h)^2 + k = 0 to obtain the real roots (if any) of a quadratic function.

nodes.label: Sketching Quadratic Functions Using Vertex Form
nodes.title: Using a(x − h)^2 + k to sketch a parabola via vertex, direction of opening, and symmetry, adding intercepts as needed.

nodes.label: Graphing Cubic Polynomial Functions y = ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d
nodes.title: Sketching general cubic polynomials by analyzing end behavior, turning points, and intercepts.

nodes.label: Graphing Exponential Functions y = a b^x
nodes.title: Plotting exponential curves with scale factor a and base b (b > 0, b ≠ 1), noting asymptotes and growth/decay.

nodes.label: Graphing Logarithmic Functions
nodes.title: Sketching y = log_b(x) and transformations, emphasizing domain x > 0 and vertical asymptote.

nodes.label: Graphing Basic Trigonometric Functions
nodes.title: Sketching y = sin x, y = cos x, and related transformations using amplitude, period, and phase shift.

nodes.label: Interpreting f(x) = g(x) as Graph Intersection
nodes.title: Understanding solutions to f(x) = g(x) as x-coordinates where the graphs of y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect.

nodes.label: Graphical Solution of f(x) = 0
nodes.title: Estimating roots by finding x-intercepts of the graph of y = f(x).

nodes.label: Graphical Solution of f(x) = k
nodes.title: Estimating solutions where the graph of y = f(x) meets the horizontal line y = k.

nodes.label: Graphical Solution of f(x) = g(x)
nodes.title: Estimating solutions by locating intersections of y = f(x) and y = g(x) on the same axes.

nodes.label: Identifying Injective Functions
nodes.title: Determining when a function is one-to-one, so distinct inputs produce distinct outputs.

nodes.label: Identifying Surjective Functions
nodes.title: Determining when a function is onto, so every element of the codomain has a preimage in the domain.

nodes.label: Identifying Bijective Functions
nodes.title: Recognizing functions that are both injective and surjective, enabling well-defined inverses.

nodes.label: Finding the Inverse of a Bijective Function
nodes.title: Algebraically deriving f^{-1}(x) by solving y = f(x) for x and interchanging variables, with domain–range swaps.

nodes.label: Sketching the Graph of an Inverse Function
nodes.title: Drawing the inverse function by reflecting the graph of y = f(x) across the line y = x.

nodes.label: Informal Concept of the Limit of a Function
nodes.title: Exploring the value a function approaches near a point using graphical and numerical reasoning.

nodes.label: Informal Concept of Continuity of a Function
nodes.title: Recognizing when a function has no breaks, jumps, or holes in its graph at a point or on an interval.

nodes.label: Limit Definition of the Derivative (First Principles)
nodes.title: Using f'(x) = lim_{h→0} [f(x+h) − f(x)]/h to differentiate basic functions, especially linear and quadratic.

nodes.label: Power Rule for Differentiation (Rational Exponents)
nodes.title: Differentiating x^a with a in Q using d/dx x^a = a x^{a−1}, covering linear, quadratic, and cubic polynomials.

nodes.label: Chain Rule
nodes.title: Differentiating a composition of functions: (f∘g)'(x) = f'(g(x))·g'(x).

nodes.label: Product Rule
nodes.title: Differentiating a product: (fg)' = f'g + fg'.

nodes.label: Quotient Rule
nodes.title: Differentiating a quotient: (f/g)' = (f'g − fg')/g^2, g ≠ 0.

nodes.label: Derivative of Exponential Functions
nodes.title: d/dx a^x = a^x ln a for a > 0; special case d/dx e^x = e^x.

nodes.label: Derivative of Logarithmic Functions
nodes.title: d/dx ln x = 1/x and d/dx log_a x = 1/(x ln a), x > 0.

nodes.label: Derivative of Inverse Functions
nodes.title: If y = f(x) is invertible, then (f^{-1})'(y) = 1 / f'(x) evaluated at x = f^{-1}(y); includes derivatives of arcsin, arctan, etc.

nodes.label: Derivative as Slope of a Tangent Line
nodes.title: Interpreting f'(a) as the gradient of the tangent line to y = f(x) at x = a.

nodes.label: Rates of Change via Derivatives
nodes.title: Using the derivative to represent instantaneous rate of change with appropriate units in context.

nodes.label: Finding Local Maxima and Minima Using Derivatives
nodes.title: Locating critical points where f' = 0 or undefined and determining extrema using first/second derivative information.

nodes.label: Curve Sketching Using First and Second Derivatives
nodes.title: Analyzing increasing/decreasing behavior, concavity, inflection points, and key features to sketch graphs.

nodes.label: Computing Second Derivatives of Polynomial Functions
nodes.title: Applying the power rule twice to find f''(x) for linear, quadratic, and cubic functions.

nodes.label: Tangent Slope to a Circle via Differentiation
nodes.title: Finding dy/dx for x^2 + y^2 = r^2 (e.g., dy/dx = −x/y) to compute the tangent slope at a point on the circle.

nodes.label: Integration as the Reverse Process of Differentiation
nodes.title: Recognizing antiderivatives: F'(x) = f(x) implies ∫ f(x) dx = F(x) + C.

nodes.label: Power Rule for Integration (Rational Exponents)
nodes.title: ∫ x^a dx = x^{a+1}/(a+1) + C for a ≠ −1, with a in Q; includes ∫ x^{−1} dx = ln|x| + C as a special case.

nodes.label: Integral of Exponential Functions
nodes.title: ∫ a^x dx = a^x/ln a + C for a > 0, a ≠ 1; special case ∫ e^x dx = e^x + C.

nodes.label: Integrals of Sine and Cosine with Linear Argument
nodes.title: ∫ sin(ax) dx = −cos(ax)/a + C and ∫ cos(ax) dx = sin(ax)/a + C for real a.

nodes.label: Area of Plane Regions via Definite Integrals
nodes.title: Using definite integrals to find area under curves and between polynomial or exponential graphs over an interval.
